newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia shares seen off highs, quiet open next week.
newsitem.headline: Russia shares seen off highs, quiet open next week.

text.p: Leading Russian shares drifted lower in late afternoon trading on Friday, coming down from a new record high earlier in the day as profit-taking set in.
Most dealers saw the market closing slightly below Thursday and forecast a quiet start to next week.
The Russian Trading System 22-share index had risen to 569.23 at 1100 GMT after finishing Thursday at a record close of 559.86.

"We've certainly seen the high for the day -- we'll finish lower than this morning on the order of two or three percent," said Rinaco-Plus trader Tom Brackenbury, saying prices had fluctuated within a two percent range all day.
"The day was somewhat sleepier than yesterday -- there has been a reasonable amount of activity, but not as much as yesterday."

National power company UES, which announced earlier in the day it would issue convertible bonds by November 20, eased to $0.4515 at 1350 GMT after $0.4635 on Thursday, while oil company LUKoil ticked down to $27.90 from $28.02.

Regional utility Irkutskenergo said it planned to place a $150 million Eurobond by the end of the year and had mandated SBC Warburg to lead the issue. Its share price was $0.379 after $0.390 previously.

"Unified Energy Systems (convertible bond) has been pending for so long," Brackenbury said, explaining the lack of movement following the announcements. "Irkutsk was less well known, but we still didn't see any price movement."
Dealers said interest was strong on second-tier less-liquid stocks, noting especially manufacturers Kirovsky Zavod and Elektrosila as well as a range of oil producers and refineries.
Brunswick director Martin Diggle said he saw some profit taking by short-term investors on both tiers.
"The market is still in good shape and there is underlying demand from Western investors," he said. "But the profit taking should put some limit on the upside to the market in the very short term."
